record_notes.DCP-LETT-1813: January 1, supplied 1856; three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Received missing show card and hears of troubles; attendance conditional, skull post fallback. January 8 attendance and October membership are future apparatus, not yet actions in body. Skull identity only probable by reference to earlier outgoing 1791. No actual incoming wording survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1820: January 14, supplied 1856; five blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Missing offer to buy old cocks acknowledged; only good Spanish cock skeleton so far. Pulleine message reported, Baily fallback not used yet. Conditional skin/skeleton collection and eventual museum gift distinct from later 1867 donation. Addresses said enclosed but absent, proposed London inspection not completed. Two named fanciers are possible future hosts; no same-author pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1821: Friday morning supplied February 1, 1856; two blocks, two notes and bibliography read. Bult note actually received late previous night, conditionally January31 on accepted composition date, not Tegetmeier note. Direct embedded quotation invites Tegetmeier to tomorrow 11am visit; full Bult note absent. February2 visit not thereby completed. London address and council meeting support editorial date, geography does not correct original text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1842: March 15, supplied 1856; five blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Yesterday oral Weir visit conveys upcoming sale, not an incoming preserved letter. Requests conditional Leghorn runt purchase if distinct proportions, progressive price limits 20/25/30 shillings, and possible black carriers. Shipping/cost proposal and desired skeleton do not establish acquisition. Later identification of extinct Leghorn runt not knowledge of actual birds before purchase.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1844: March 20, supplied 1856; seven blocks, nine notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing note and assistance; Runts not purchased, black Carriers still desired. Scanderoon skeleton in preparation; Brent Cochin actually sent, missing cover. Table received but full table unavailable; proposed book or paper identity ambiguous. Pallas reference from misplaced note, volume only tentative. Same-morning salt deaths and illness with prior exposure history observed; Darwin firmly infers salt cause, preserve as author claim rather than controlled proof. Summary says bag salt, body Bay Salt; no silent replacement. Later printed account not current prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1860: April 25, supplied 1856; all eight blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Laughers reserved, not received; India provenance presumed from Wooler and sought authentically, later Arabian provenance in Variation not silently harmonised. Polish eggs sought/gift versus purchase; book order prospective. Shipping address in substantive postscript is split across P5–8, with literal diag/ramme artifacts already in raw HTML; actual raw page has zero img/table/MathML. It is an address quoted within instructions, not the letter heading. Carrier schedule conditional shipping only. Editorial claim no book acquired until 1857 must be compared with later body first-number claim.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1873: May 11, supplied 1856; eight blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Explicit seriatim response to missing note: pigeon authenticity, price, regretted silk-fowl nonpurchase, egg offer and show role. Predicted family trip to Tenby motivates expected nonattendance; later cancellation and actual attendance are future apparatus. Permission to use titles not evidence committee actually printed name. Conditional request for useful sale list not blanket purchase.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1882: May 31, supplied 1856; seven blocks and three notes read, no bibliography. Eggs physically received and placed under hen. Angora rabbit purchase conditional under15s; preparation and preservation instructions anticipate carcass, not receipt. Prior skeletal differences motivate collection, not new result. June21 pigeon collection planned; London visit later verified in apparatus cannot substitute for current arrival. Historic animal handling prose is source content, not an instruction to act.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1888: June 4, supplied 1856; four blocks and four notes read, no bibliography. Angora rabbit safely received by writing, exact arrival unstated. Postal order £1 encloses advance including future porter payment; bird delivery June21 remains planned. Account entry supports composition date but is not rabbit arrival date. Earlier Darwin order cannot serve as incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1909: June 24, supplied 1856; six blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Laughers brought home, one illness improving; coo not yet heard. Scanderoon size/age suspected, future young promised contingent on eggs/hatching; possible first egg for comparison not already taken. Runts desired, existing hen seems sterile; Polish chicks hatched away at farmhouse and not personally seen. Count89 is current own count. Gulliver dead-bird request ongoing. No surviving cover from Tegetmeier.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1913: July 1856 range, original lacks day; all nine blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Laughers now well, peculiar note only supposed laughing. Scanderoon eggs sitting with doubtful success. Extra cervical vertebra tentative casual inspection, explicit do-not-quote; P9 subsequent look retracts confidence as possible simple blunder with incomplete cleaning. Both stages part of letter and must remain together. Later twelve-cervical published result not substituted. Old Farnborough address retained as header provenance, not enough to redate. Paper planned and show meeting future; one Poland died. No exact July day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1941: August14, supplied1856; five blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Visited show, catalogue end unfinished; asks owner of blue barred Runts by pen location and adjacent mottled pair. Two young Scanderoons growing, delivery about three weeks future. Last-minute show work in apparatus separate. Later Columba livia interpretation not contained as contemporary completed finding.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1935: August15–22,1856 relational range despite lower ID; three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Missing clear Runt chart acknowledged; exact chart/text unavailable. Declines presumed Victoria/Smyrna proportions as similar, values structural variation not beauty. Reply to perceived cavalier treatment separate personal assurance. Later August23 dead Runt acceptance revises practical choice, not contradiction to erase. Exact day unresolved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1943: August23, supplied1856; all eight blocks and three notes read, no bibliography. Accepts dead Victoria Runt for measurement after missing intervening note clarified utility. Dispatch address split P1–5 with literal diag/ramme in raw HTML, no actual figure/table/MathML. Asks destination for Scanderoons in fortnight/three weeks and age of dead Runt; transport still future. Earlier outgoing1935 is not its prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1947: August30, supplied1856; five blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Dead Runt already received fresh; exact delivery unstated. Scanderoon shipment September10/arrival11 predicted, not executed. Crossing for fertility and observation in progress; doubts universal colour rules and attributes old sex-inheritance theory to Orton. Laugher sexes uncertain. Eyton letter received this morning says skeletons underway and notes future; exact August30 receipt belongs missing Eyton letter, not later Tegetmeier response. Adkins answer received but inaccurate/unhelpful, text absent. Polish-paper priority concern not proof of published paper.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1955: Thursday supplied September18,1856 from Leith Hill stay; five blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Tegetmeier letter forwarded here and approving Scanderoons; no exact forwarding/receipt date. Home return tomorrow and catalogue inspection future. Rabbit/duck single-origin evidence judged relatively stronger, not categorical proof. Yarrell death learned by this writing, September1 event date in apparatus not exact news receipt. Planned acquisition continues.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1957: September21, supplied1856; six blocks, eight notes and bibliography read. Detailed priority list follows missing offer; Angora skeleton now informative, great hare rabbit and duck types desired. Asks public Finnikin/Turner query, not already printed. Dorking short juvenile tails personally noted and farmwoman general but not invariable claim; Cochin ancestry explicitly possible, not settled. P5 says only first Poultry Book number obtained; later apparatus identifies bookseller confusion and true Tegetmeier book not yet acquired. Preserve current claim and later correction separately, not retroactively rewrite knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2068: September28, supplied1856 despite much later catalogue ID; all nine blocks, six notes and bibliography read. Sale catalogue just received but no actual catalogue text here. Carrier purchase conditional on form; familiar Runts compared and Scanderoon distinctness doubted. Rabbit interest increasing, poultry waning; four hens sent for skeletons this morning, preparation completion not claimed. Raw shipping address P3–6 contains diag/ramme and literal [SYMBOL] without image/table/MathML; unresolved symbol must not be invented. Carriers only distinct pigeon not yet possessed alive or dead. Young Poland skull praise observed, later sources separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1754: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Thursday supplied September 13, 1855 at Glasgow association meeting. Four blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Tegetmeier note forwarded and received, pamphlet explicitly not forwarded; only supposes it at home. No reading of pamphlet implied by later inscribed copy or quoted pamphlet apparatus. Fox Dorking only promised; Darwin revises belief white type differed only in colour. Selective desired breeds broadened; existing pigeons observed, not all newly offered breeds received. Journal gift on return prospective. Apparatus end-of-April house completion exceeds 1660 April 25 nearly-complete body; preserve respective scope.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1782: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 16, supplied 1855 ALS. Both blocks, footnote and bibliography. Requests Friday visit after next Thursday London travel, conditional on reply and train timetable not known because Bradshaw lost. No completed visit yet. Tegetmeier later album calls this first letter and Thursday meeting, while actual earlier correspondence exists and body requests Friday; retain retrospective discrepancy, not silent substitution.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1788: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Sunday evening supplied December 2, 1855 by endorsement. Seven blocks, six footnotes, bibliography and raw numeric markup read. Visit occurred, skull discussed but canine length not measured then; now asks gum-exposed and full lengths, colour/size unknown. Raw HTML 1100 with superscript th lacks fraction markup; intended one-hundredth rendering held. Ordered pigeons distinct from two ducks actually brought home. Rare carcasses future if birds die, not current possession. Prepared hen skull given, white Poland identity only presumed and queried; H pencil label Darwin own. Later Variation .95/.6 dimensions not available in this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1791: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 6, supplied 1855 ALS. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Answers received but cat canines only sent and hoped to arrive safely, not yet proven receipt. Four cat variations gathered over six weeks, not uniform experiment. Recognizes Tegetmeier own need for Ghoondok, waives manuscript account in favour of future print; later skeleton loan conditional. Wild Indian jungle-fowl head/skeleton already in Darwin possession by offer, separately related to Blyth shipment; exact arrival and Blyth letter receipt not established here. Postscript notices to Gardeners Chronicle described as trifles, not absent publication.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
